title: Quantitative and interface-aware prediction of peptide–protein interactions by VITAL - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
AbstractThe quantitative characterization of peptide–protein interactions remains a persistent challenge in computational biology, limiting mechanistic insight and therapeutic development. Here we introduce VITAL (Versatile InTerface-Aware global-local co-Learning), a deep learning framework built on a dual-channel co-learning architecture that fuses protein language model embeddings with a geometry-aware encoder capturing spatial proximity at the interface. This integrated learning strategy enables the simultaneous prediction of peptide–protein interactions, interface mapping and quantitative affinity estimation. We report that VITAL advances the field through three key contributions. First, VITAL reaches state-of-the-art accuracy (max AUC = 0.87) across diverse benchmarks, with experimental validation of selected novel interactions in a real-world peptide discovery attempt. Second, we demonstrate near-residue-resolution interface mapping (>60% precision), which facilitates systematic classification of four fundamental binding modes. Finally, we present the binding strength unit, a continuous affinity metric that correlates significantly with experimental data. By unifying high-resolution structural profiling with quantitative scoring, VITAL establishes a scalable computational platform that accelerates the transition from qualitative screening to quantitative, structure-informed analysis. This streamlines the discovery and design of peptide-based therapeutics. The model is publicly available as an open-source package and interactive web server to promote community adoption and further methodological innovation.

Data availability

The datasets generated and/or analysed during the current study are available via GitHub at https://github.com/BADDxmu/VITAL.
Code availability

The VITAL framework is available as an open-source package via GitHub (https://github.com/BADDxmu/VITAL), with the version used in this study archived on Zenodo45 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20797353). A publicly accessible interactive web server is also available at https://www.vital-peppi.online/ to facilitate use and adoption by the community.
